messages:
keiko: hey @people-ops — quick question. i’m due back from parental leave on 2025-07-15 but my partner just had emergency surgery. i need to be primary caregiver for ~6 extra weeks. what’s the process for requesting unpaid extension? will benefits, equity vesting, or my work visa be affected?

ben-peopleops: sorry to hear that, keiko — hope they recover quickly. you can request an unpaid extension; we call it a compassionate LOA extension. steps below. happy to help walk through. :heart:

maria-benefits: hi all — quick bullets on benefits:
• short-term health coverage: we can continue employer coverage for up to 60 days of unpaid leave if you sign the benefits continuation form; beyond that you’ll need to elect COBRA.
• payroll deductions: if coverage continues, you’ll still need to cover your portion of premiums (payroll deduction or invoiced).
• 401(k): employer match pauses during unpaid leave longer than one full pay period. your vesting schedule is unchanged.
• equity refresh/bonus eligibility: these are handled case-by-case — manager + comp committee sign-off for prorated bonus eligibility.

james: keiko — we’ll absolutely support this. from a team side i can approve the extension and arrange coverage for your on-call weeks. please submit the LOA extension form and CC me.

keiko: thanks — what exact paperwork? and any sample wording i can send to my manager?

ben-peopleops: paperwork = 1) LOA extension form (people-ops link), 2) benefits continuation form (for health), 3) if on a visa, immigration notification form. i’ve pasted a short manager email you can copy below.

ben-peopleops: ```
Subject: Request for unpaid LOA extension (compassionate)

Hi James,

I’m currently scheduled to return from parental leave on 2025-07-15. Due to my partner’s recent surgery, I’d like to request an unpaid extension of leave from 2025-07-15 through 2025-08-26 (6 weeks). I am requesting manager approval to extend my LOA and for guidance on any impact to benefits or payroll. I can be reached at +1-555-0123 if needed.

Thanks,
Keiko
```

payroll-bot: @ben-peopleops noted. when manager approval is received, payroll will create an unpaid leave action and stop salary payments effective 2025-07-15. please confirm benefits continuation option selection to avoid coverage lapse.

maria-benefits: also add: if you elect benefits continuation via company plan, we’ll invoice you monthly for your share — enroll via the benefits form within 14 days of the last paid paycheck.

keiko: i’m on an H-1B — the visa question worries me. what happens if i’m unpaid?

hr-bot: H-1B holders: unpaid leave beyond 30 days may have visa implications. please schedule an immigration consult with our legal partner immediately. we can also issue a letter confirming approved leave dates if needed for USCIS.

tara-former-parent: fwiw i did a 4-week unpaid extension last year for a similar reason. manager approved, benefits continued for 45 days via company admin, and i had to temporarily suspend 401k deferrals. immigration was fine after we submitted the leave letter. happy to DM the steps.

keiko: this is super helpful, thank you. last Q: does unpaid extension count toward job protection (i.e., can i be held to same position)?

ben-peopleops: job protection: we aim to hold your role or equivalent. for leaves longer than 12 weeks there’s more nuance; 6 weeks is within our typical accommodation window. we’ll document everything in the LOA record.

keiko: perfect. i’ll submit the LOA extension form now and use the template — cc-ing james. appreciate everyone. :pray:

james: thanks keiko — once you submit i’ll approve and we’ll coordinate with payroll/benefits. take the time you need.

payroll-bot: ticket #LOA-4821 created for keiko — payroll action pending manager approval.

ben-peopleops: tagging @maria-benefits to watch for the enrollment form. keiko, ping me if you want me to draft the official leave letter for immigration.

keiko: will do, thanks again!
